content.text: I reviewed the complete package: disclosure, brief, all USER passages in the conversation, all ten draft sections, the numeral table, and all six figure briefs.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. Every limitation of claims 1-20 (device 1-10, system 11-15, method 16-20) traces to affirmative disclosure text: rigid base with first/second sides, vibration motor on the first side, air-extraction mechanism such as a vacuum pump on the first side in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side, rigid low-friction loop or skirt at the perimeter (plastic, metal, PTFE, combinations of rigid materials), deliberate absence of an airtight seal with air entering beneath the rigid perimeter, continuous extraction maintaining the chamber below atmospheric pressure, the resulting pressure differential holding the device without operator downforce, rigid-path vibration transfer with substantially less damping than a flexible suction cup, free sliding to successive areas while the vacuum maintains contact, guiding handles, and the rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled position-versus-hold control. Claim 10 and the FIG. 6 third embodiment (stirring elements, vibration-driven constant forward motion, no pulling or hand guidance needed) trace to the one affirmative USER technical passage in the conversation; all other conversation turns are operational resume/repair instructions and were treated as non-supporting, as were the drafting agent's own YOU passages. All seventeen numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) were checked: each has exactly one meaning across the numeral table, the detailed description and every brief, and each appears on at least one sheet. Section designations were checked in all three places for both cuts: FIG. 3's brief creates "2-2" and "4-4", FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 briefs are taken on those same lines, and the Brief Description of the Drawings repeats the same designations. Brief Description paragraphs for FIGS. 1-6 were compared line by line against the corresponding authoritative briefs (sectioned versus elevation bodies, omitted parts, schematic recitals) and agree. Depiction conventions (rectangular plan form, band depth, block order, port width/position, flat lower end of the perimeter member, stirring-element number and placement) are all confined to the figure briefs and none is verbalized in the application text as an example embodiment or an "any closed outline" broadening; no undisclosed taper, angle, runout, deeper-end, or contact-topology statement was found on the bearing face, clearance or port. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, or unresolved alternative remains in any draft section. One verified internal inconsistency was found, in the FIG. 5 brief's numeral lists, and is reported with a filing-clean fix; the citation markers in the Background are prior-art characterizations reserved for the later citation review and are not reported here.

findings.title: FIG. 5 brief lists numeral 24 as shown on the sheet although the sheet defines no callout for it
findings.where: figures/FIG-5-SECOND-EMBODIMENT-WITH-A-PULLING-ELEMENT.md, trailing "## Numerals shown on this figure" list, compared with the same file's callout bullets and "**Numerals appearing on this figure:**" line
findings.detail: The FIG. 5 brief carries two numeral lists that disagree. The authoritative annotation line reads "**Numerals appearing on this figure:** 10, 36, 46", and the callout bullets define exactly three targets: the vibration device 10 on the outer boundary line at the right-hand end of the rectangular body, the flexible pulling element 46 on the slack curved path, and the covering element 36 in the open stretch of tile. The trailing list, however, adds 24. No bullet in the FIG. 5 brief identifies a target, leader endpoint or reference surface for the perimeter member 24 on this sheet, so numeral 24 as listed is unanchored: annotating it would place a numeral with no defined callout, and leaving it in the list contradicts the brief's own annotation line. Every other figure brief (FIGS. 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6) has the two lists in exact agreement, which confirms the FIG. 5 trailing list is the outlier rather than the annotation line. This is a text-internal inconsistency only; the underlying depiction is unaffected, because the band is drawn in the geometry and the Brief Description of the Drawings properly says of FIG. 5 that "the vibration device, the perimeter member, the covering element, the flexible pulling element and the connection of the flexible pulling element to the vibration device being shown schematically" without requiring that the perimeter member be numbered on that sheet (it is numbered 24 on FIGS. 1, 2, 3 and 4).
findings.evidence:
FIG. 5 brief, annotation line: "**Numerals appearing on this figure:** 10, 36, 46". FIG. 5 brief, callout bullets: "- The vibration device 10 is the whole machine standing on the covering element 36 ... - The flexible pulling element 46 is that slack curved path ... - The covering element 36 is that large plain tile ..." (no bullet for 24). FIG. 5 brief, trailing list: "## Numerals shown on this figure

- 10
- 24
- 36
- 46". Contrast FIG. 1, where both lists read "10, 12, 18, 20, 24, 36, 44".
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-5-SECOND-EMBODIMENT-WITH-A-PULLING-ELEMENT.md, delete the line "- 24" from the "## Numerals shown on this figure" list, so that the list reads "- 10", "- 36", "- 46" and matches the "**Numerals appearing on this figure:** 10, 36, 46" line and the three callout bullets. Make no other change: do not add a numeral 24 callout to FIG. 5, do not alter the FIG. 5 geometry, and do not alter the FIG. 5 paragraph in draft/07-drawings.md.
